title: Novel bioactive peptides alleviate Western diet-induced MAFLD in C57BL/6J mice by inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis via TLR4/NF-kappaB and Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathways.
authors: Wayal, Vipul; Wang, Shulhn-Der; Hsieh, Chang-Chi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究生物活性肽对MAFLD小鼠模型的治疗作用及信号通路机制，仅涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has emerged as a leading chronic liver disease. This condition is characterized by an abnormal accumulation of fat within liver and can progress from simple steatosis to more severe stages involving chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. In this study, we investigated the potential therapeutic effects and underlying mechanism of novel bioactive peptides (EWYF and EWFY) on Western diet-induced MAFLD in C57BL/6J mice. Mice fed a normal chow diet (ND group) and Western diet (WD and treatment groups) for 8 weeks. Treatment groups received EWYF and EWFY peptides in low (10 mg/kg/day) and high (50 mg/kg/day) doses were divided into four groups: EWYF10, EWYF50, EWFY10, and EWFY50. Western diet-induced body weight gain and increased liver weight along with visceral adiposity, which were markedly reversed by bioactive peptides in a dose-dependent manner. Additionally, bioactive peptides significantly reduced hepatic steatosis, liver injury and proinflammatory response. Western diet-induced glucose tolerance and insulin resistance, whereas bioactive peptides significantly improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity. Persistent intake of Western diet triggered chronic inflammation and severe oxidative stress, which were significantly alleviated by bioactive peptides treatment via inhibiting NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation and mitigated pyroptosis by modulating TLR4/NF-kappaB and Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathways. Furthermore, molecular docking studies suggest that EWYF and EWFY act as fructokinase antagonists and TLR4 inhibitors, which potentially alleviates Western diet-induced MAFLD. Collectively, these findings highlight EWYF and EWFY as promising candidates for MAFLD treatment due to their potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties via specific molecular inhibition.
abstract_zh: 代谢相关脂肪性肝病（MAFLD）已成为一种主要的慢性肝病。该疾病以肝脏内脂肪异常积聚为特征，并可从单纯性脂肪变性进展至涉及慢性炎症和氧化应激的更严重阶段。在本研究中，我们探讨了新型生物活性肽（EWYF和EWFY）对西方饮食诱导的C57BL/6J小鼠MAFLD的潜在治疗效应及其潜在机制。小鼠分别饲喂正常饮食（ND组）和西方饮食（WD组及治疗组）8周。治疗组接受低剂量（10 mg/kg/天）和高剂量（50 mg/kg/天）的EWYF和EWFY肽，分为四组：EWYF10、EWYF50、EWFY10和EWFY50。西方饮食诱导的体重增加、肝脏重量增加及内脏脂肪堆积，被生物活性肽以剂量依赖性方式显著逆转。此外，生物活性肽显著减少了肝脏脂肪变性、肝损伤和促炎反应。西方饮食诱导了葡萄糖耐受不良和胰岛素抵抗，而生物活性肽显著改善了葡萄糖耐受性和胰岛素敏感性。持续摄入西方饮食触发了慢性炎症和严重氧化应激，而生物活性肽治疗通过抑制NOD样受体蛋白3（NLRP3）炎症小体激活，并调节TLR4/NF-kappaB和Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1信号通路减轻细胞焦亡，从而显著缓解这些效应。此外，分子对接研究表明，EWYF和EWFY作为果糖激酶拮抗剂和TLR4抑制剂，可能缓解西方饮食诱导的MAFLD。总体而言，这些发现凸显了EWYF和EWFY因其通过特定分子抑制发挥的强效抗氧化和抗炎特性，而成为MAFLD治疗的有前景候选药物。
